title: Input-centric OFTv2 versus materialized OFT and Mirror views
hypothesis: Applying an orthogonal task transform to activations without materializing transformed weights preserves the same function and reduces adaptation/decode overhead; a small Mirror coordinate can amortize task-specific view state only for aligned task orbits.
physical_object: one frozen shared linear feature map
mirror_coordinate: one input-side Givens angle at the activation interface
logical_multiplicity: multiple task-conditioned functions from one shared physical weight matrix

development.allowed: check forward equivalence, layout, matrix orientation, timing instrumentation and payload accounting

success_gate: Input-centric output matches weight-centric OFT within 1e-6 relative error; aligned one-angle code <=50% per-task transform bytes and does not add more than 10% measured forward latency at batch 64.
failure_gate: Function mismatch >1e-4, or view payload reduction <20% at matched quality, or input-centric transform adds >25% latency.
boundaries: No CUDA or language model claim
OFTv2 is prior art; input-side orthogonality is not a Mirror novelty claim
